# Engine: `graph-execution/api` library entry and sub-path-safe run pages

## What to build

Two small changes to the engine in `packages/graph-execution/` (the repo is an npm-workspaces monorepo; the engine is the `graph-execution` workspace), so a separate app (graph-manager, in `apps/graph-manager`) can use it.

1. **Library entry `graph-execution/api`.** Add `packages/graph-execution/src/api.ts` that re-exports the pieces another Node program needs to discover and read runs, and publish it through `package.json` `exports` with type declarations. Importing it must not run the CLI. `src/cli.ts` calls `await main()` at top level, so `api.ts` must never import `cli.ts`.
2. **Relative URLs in the run page and suite page.** Today `page.html`, `runpage.js`, `suitepage.js` and `diffview.js` use absolute URLs (`/assets/…`, `/state`, `/events`, `/retry/…`, `/api/…`). Make every URL relative to the page, so the page also works when a reverse proxy serves it under a sub-path such as `/runs/ws/123/view/`.

The server side stays the same: same routes, same Host/Origin checks.

## Context: files to read before implementing

All paths are under `packages/graph-execution/`.

- `src/state/state.ts`:
  - lines 7-79: `taskStatusSchema`, `runStatusSchema`, `reviewStateSchema`, `stateSchema`; types `RunState`, `TaskStatus`, `RunStatus`
  - line 96: `StateStore.load`
  - line 160: `LOCK_FILE`
  - line 164: `isAlive(pid)`
  - line 184: `lockHolder(runDir)`
- `src/state/paths.ts` (lines 1-23): `RUNS_DIR`, `RUN_ID_ENV`, `RUN_ID_PATTERN`, `runsRoot`.
- `src/state/errors.ts` (lines 1-17): `EXIT_SUCCESS`, `EXIT_REVIEW_FAILED`, `EXIT_ABORT`, `EXIT_HANDOFF_BLOCKED`, `ExitCode`.
- `src/cleanup/scan.ts`:
  - lines 9-40: `RunKind`, `RunEntry` (`{type:"run"|"suite", id, dir, status, kind, createdAt?, sizeBytes, branches, pid?, features}`), `Scan`
  - line 139: `scan(repo)`, which reads `<repo>/.graph-execution` and the `graph*` branches; a run counts as `live` when its lock holder pid is alive
- `src/launch/open.ts` (lines 14-24): `webJsonSchema = z.object({ url, pid })`, `WebJson`, `readWebJson(runDir)`.
- `src/web/serve.ts`: `webJsonPath(runDir)`, i.e. `<runDir>/web.json`, written while a `--web` run's server is up.
- `src/suite/state.ts`: `suiteStateSchema`, `SUITE_FILE`.
- `src/ui/store.ts` (lines 8-112): `NodeStatus`, `NodeView`, `ViewState`, the live snapshot the page renders.
- `src/web/page.html` and `src/suite/page.html`: `<link href="/assets/…">` and `<script src="/assets/runpage.js">`.
- `src/web/assets/runpage.js`:
  - lines 1-7: `import … from "/assets/util.js"`
  - fetches at lines 132, 142, 150, 188, 245, 249, 261, 410, 414, 456
  - line 459: `new EventSource("/events")`
- `src/web/assets/suitepage.js`: about 19 absolute URLs (`/api/suite`, `/api/features/…/events`, `/assets/…`).
- `src/web/assets/diffview.js` (line 177): `import("/assets/vendor/highlight/highlight.min.js")`.
- `src/web/assets/review.js`: already uses relative imports (`./diffview.js`). Check how it builds its API URLs (`reviewApi`) and make those relative too.
- `src/web/server.test.ts` (line 129) asserts the page contains `/assets/runpage.js`. Update it to the new relative form.
- `src/web/assets.ts`: serves `GET /assets/<path>`. Unchanged.
- `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.build.json` and `package.json` (`bin`, `files`, `scripts.build`).

## Patterns to follow

**Relative URLs:**
- Module imports inside `assets/*.js` become `./util.js`, resolved against the module's own URL.
- In HTML, `href="assets/theme.css"` and `src="assets/runpage.js"`, without a leading slash.
- Fetches become `fetch("state")`, `fetch("retry/" + encodeURIComponent(id), …)`, `new EventSource("events")`, `fetch("api/suite")`. These resolve against the document URL.
- The page is always served at a path ending in `/`. The server serves `GET /` already. A proxy maps `/prefix/…/view/` to `/`.
- Dynamic `import("/assets/vendor/…")` in `diffview.js` becomes `import("./vendor/highlight/highlight.min.js")`, resolved against diffview.js.

**Library entry, `src/api.ts`:**
```ts
// Public, stable surface for programs that read graph-execution runs (graph-manager). Never import cli.ts here.
export { stateSchema, runStatusSchema, taskStatusSchema, lockHolder, isAlive, LOCK_FILE, type RunState, type RunStatus, type TaskStatus } from "./state/state.js";
export { RUNS_DIR, RUN_ID_ENV, RUN_ID_PATTERN, runsRoot } from "./state/paths.js";
export { scan, type RunEntry, type RunKind, type Scan } from "./cleanup/scan.js";
export { readWebJson, type WebJson } from "./launch/open.js";
export { webJsonPath } from "./web/serve.js";
export { suiteStateSchema, SUITE_FILE } from "./suite/state.js";
export type { NodeStatus, NodeView, ViewState } from "./ui/store.js";
export { EXIT_SUCCESS, EXIT_REVIEW_FAILED, EXIT_ABORT, EXIT_HANDOFF_BLOCKED, type ExitCode } from "./state/errors.js";
/** Absolute path of the CLI entry, for programs that spawn it. */
export const CLI_PATH: string = fileURLToPath(new URL("./cli.js", import.meta.url));
```
- Add the `fileURLToPath` import.
- Check each re-exported name exists with exactly that name. Use the real names if they differ.
- Check that no module in this import closure runs side effects at import time (spawning, `process.exit`). If `launch/open.ts` pulls in too much, move `readWebJson` and its schema into a small new module, `src/web/webjson.ts`, and import it from both places.

**package.json:**
```json
"exports": {
  ".": "./dist/cli.js",
  "./api": { "types": "./dist/api.d.ts", "import": "./dist/api.js" },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
- Set `"declaration": true` in `tsconfig.build.json`. Declarations only need to be correct for `api.ts` and its import closure, but emitting them for everything is fine.
- Keep `bin` as it is.
- Keep the `"."` export so `import("graph-execution")` stays what it was. The bin is not affected by `exports`.

**Test pattern:** vitest. The tests run after `vitest.global-setup.ts` has built `dist/`. See `src/env.test.ts` (lines 7-29): it spawns `node -e 'import "./dist/env.js"'` with `cwd` set to the package root and checks the output.

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `packages/graph-execution/src/api.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: as above.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build -w graph-execution && ls packages/graph-execution/dist/api.js packages/graph-execution/dist/api.d.ts`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/package.json` and `tsconfig.build.json`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `exports` as above; `declaration: true`.
- **GOTCHA**: `src/e2e.test.ts` asserts the packed tarball's top-level entries. The `dist/*.d.ts` files live inside `dist`, so the assertion still holds.

### CREATE `packages/graph-execution/src/api.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - Spawn `node --input-type=module -e "import * as api from 'graph-execution/api'; console.log(JSON.stringify(Object.keys(api).sort()))"` with `cwd` = the repo root, two levels above the package. Workspaces symlink `node_modules/graph-execution`, so the self-reference resolves through `exports`.
  - Assert the key list contains `stateSchema`, `scan`, `lockHolder`, `readWebJson`, `EXIT_ABORT`, `CLI_PATH`.
  - Assert the process exits 0 within 5 s and prints no CLI help. This shows importing it does not run the CLI.
  - A second test: create a temp git repo (use `tempRepo()` from `src/__fixtures__/repo.ts`), write `.graph-execution/r1/state.json` with a minimal valid state, parsed through `stateSchema` so the shape is right. Then call `scan(repo)` through the dist import and assert one run `r1` comes back.

### UPDATE web assets and pages to relative URLs

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `src/web/page.html`, `src/suite/page.html`: every `/assets/…` becomes `assets/…`.
  - `src/web/assets/runpage.js`, `src/web/assets/suitepage.js`, `src/web/assets/diffview.js`, `review.js`, `logs.js`, `shell.js` and any other asset: replace absolute imports and fetch/EventSource URLs with relative ones as described above.
  - Grep afterwards: `grep -rn "\"/assets\|'/assets\|fetch(\"/\|EventSource(\"/\|\"/api/" packages/graph-execution/src/web packages/graph-execution/src/suite` must find nothing outside tests.
- **GOTCHA**: URLs built by string concatenation, such as `"/retry/" + id`, become `"retry/" + id`. Do not use `new URL("/x", location)`.

### CREATE a sub-path regression test

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `src/web/server.test.ts`:
  - Start the run web server the way the existing tests do.
  - Start a tiny `http` proxy on 127.0.0.1 that maps `/p/q/<rest>` to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<rest>`, sets the `Host` header to `127.0.0.1:<port>` and drops `Origin`.
  - `GET /p/q/` through the proxy returns the page.
  - For every `href="…"`/`src="…"` in it, resolve it against `http://proxy/p/q/` and GET it through the proxy: each returns 200.
  - `GET /p/q/state` returns JSON with `runId`.
  - Update the existing assertion at line 129 to `assets/runpage.js`.
- Do the same page check for the suite server in `src/suite/server.test.ts`, if it has a test that fetches the page.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `import { stateSchema, scan, readWebJson, lockHolder, CLI_PATH } from "graph-execution/api"` works from another workspace, with types, and does not run the CLI.
- [ ] The run page and the suite page load their assets, state and SSE events both at `/` and through a sub-path proxy.
- [ ] No absolute `/assets`, `/state`, `/events`, `/api/` URLs remain in `src/web/assets/*.js`, `src/web/page.html` or `src/suite/page.html`.
- [ ] The existing web tests pass, including `src/web-e2e.test.ts` and `src/suite/web-e2e.test.ts`.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` at the repo root pass.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build -w graph-execution
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-execution -- src/api.test.ts src/web src/suite
npm test
```
